statement: CoWoS allocation, not HBM supply, is described as the binding constraint on AI system availability, with capacity around 105,000-130,000 wafers per month by Q4 2026.
why: Identifying which link in the chain binds tells you where added GPU output can and cannot come from over the next few quarters.

impact.mechanism: If packaging allocation is the bottleneck, incremental HBM or wafer starts do not raise finished accelerator supply until packaging capacity expands, so system availability tracks CoWoS ramp rather than memory output.

evidence.excerpt: CoWoS allocation is the binding constraint on system availability, not HBM supply.

confidence.basis: Secondary newsletter analysis citing a bank estimate for the capacity figure; no primary foundry confirmation, so capped at medium.

dispersion: Capacity given as a range of ~105,000-130,000 wafers/month attributed to JPMorgan; the binding-constraint call is the newsletter's own judgement.
